# odr-dabmod

**Turns a DAB ensemble into a transmittable OFDM signal**

- **Version recorded:** 3.0.0
- **Categories:** `sdr`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/Opendigitalradio/ODR-DabMod>
- **Not a recommended default** — installed only when asked for.

## What it does

Takes an ETI stream and produces the DAB OFDM waveform from it, with the digital predistortion and gain control a real transmitter chain needs, and delivers it to a USRP or other SDR, to a file, or over the network.

## Why you would want it

It is the modulator half of the free-software DAB transmission chain, and the piece that makes small-scale and community DAB possible without broadcast-grade hardware. Several licensed small-scale DAB operators run exactly this.

## Before it will work

An ETI stream from odr-dabmux. Transmitting hardware, and -- this is the part that is not a technical prerequisite -- a licence. Small-scale DAB licensing exists in a number of countries and is the route by which this software is normally used.

## How it installs

- apt: `odr-dabmod`

## Known problems

This is the component that emits. DAB Band III is allocated to broadcasting and radiating into it without authorisation interferes with a licensed service over a wide area, because that is what the standard is designed to do. This project discloses the capability and does not tell you what your jurisdiction permits (D-021). Predistortion tuning against a real amplifier is the hard part of using it well and is not something the defaults accomplish.
